financials.structural_notes: FINANCING STRUCTURE (10-K, FY2025): CoreWeave "primarily finance[s] our infrastructure development through asset-level debt supported by take-or-pay customer contracts, supplemented by corporate-level equity and debt financing." The asset-level debt is the family of Delayed Draw Term Loan ("DDTL") Facilities (DDTL 1.0/2.0/2.1/3.0). Per Note 10—Debt: "The total loans available provided by the DDTL Facilities are constrained by the purchase price of assets for which the loans are being used to finance with such percentage based upon the depreciable cost of graphics processing unit ('GPU') servers." GPU/ASSET COLLATERAL + SPV-STYLE RING-FENCING: "Obligations outstanding under the DDTL Facilities are secured by perfected first priority pledges of and security interests in (i) the equity interests of the respective subsidiaries held by its direct parent and (ii) substantially all of the assets of the respective subsidiaries" — i.e. financing is pushed down into asset-holding subsidiaries whose equity and assets (the GPU servers) are pledged. The DDTLs "require the maintenance of restricted cash balances based on a percentage of drawn amounts" (the 10-K reports $819M current + $184M non-current restricted cash; MD&A: "$1.0 billion of restricted cash... related to a collateralized loan facility"). PARENT GUARANTEE SCOPE: "all obligations under the DDTL Facilities are unconditionally guaranteed by the Company [CoreWeave, Inc.]" — the parent guarantee makes this recourse to the parent, NOT a bankruptcy-remote off-balance-sheet structure; all of this debt is consolidated on CoreWeave's balance sheet. The 10-K exhibit list shows multiple "Parent Guarantee and Pledge Agreement" documents (e.g. dated July 30 2023, May 16 2024, July 28 2025 via CCAC VII Holdco LLC) plus the Revolving Credit Facility ("secured by pledges of certain assets as collateral") and 2030/2031 Senior Notes and 2031 Convertible Senior Notes at the corporate level. SINGLE-CUSTOMER TAKE-OR-PAY CONCENTRATION: "Customers generally access our platform through multi-year committed contracts, under which they purchase a specified amount of capacity on a take-or-pay basis." Revenue is highly concentrated: "We recognized an aggregate of approximately 67% of our revenue from our top customer, Microsoft, for the year ended December 31, 2025." Large future take-or-pay commitments: OpenAI up to ~$6.5B through May 31, 2031 (Sept 2025 order; an earlier MSA committed up to ~$11.9B through Oct 2030) and Meta up to ~$14.2B through Dec 2031; total remaining performance obligations (RPO) of $60.7B at 12/31/2025 vs $15.1B at 12/31/2024, weighted-average contract duration ~5 years. NOTE on "bankruptcy-remote/SPV": the 10-K does NOT use the term "bankruptcy-remote" or "special purpose entity"; the subsidiary-pledge + unconditional parent guarantee structure is the relevant analogue and is fully recourse/consolidated, so downside flows to the parent.

SINGLE-CUSTOMER MEGA-CONTRACT (Microsoft): On Nov 2, 2025 IREN signed a 5-year (average term) agreement with Microsoft Corporation for dedicated GPU services at Childress, TX with total contract value ~$9.7 billion, "with 20% of the contract value to be paid prior to the applicable delivery date of each tranche" (i.e., large prepayments rather than classic take-or-pay; this single contract dominates IREN's HPC/AI revenue ramp). As of Mar 31, 2026, nil Microsoft tranches had been delivered/accepted, so $0 of the $9.7B is yet in RPO; total unsatisfied RPO was only $710.3M. Customer concentration is a stated risk factor.

GPU/ASSET COLLATERAL & DEBT-FINANCED GPUs: During 9mo FY2026 IREN entered GPU lease-financing arrangements that "provide financing for 100% of the purchase price," structured as 24- and 36-month finance leases ($274.256M finance-lease liability at Mar 31, 2026; GPU hardware on balance sheet grew to $811.4M gross plus $301.8M finance-lease ROU). Separately, on Nov 5, 2025 IREN entered a $199.8M Dell Financial Services 24-month GPU lease facility ($1 purchase option); "The Company has agreed to provide a parent guarantee with respect to all payment obligations under this facility." IREN also "unconditionally guarantee[s] the obligations of IE CA Leasing and IE US Hardware 1 under the Dell Purchase Agreements." 

PROPOSED $3.6B SECURED MICROSOFT FACILITY (undrawn): Feb 4, 2026 binding commitment letter from Goldman Sachs Bank USA and JPMorgan to underwrite ~$3.6B delayed-draw financing for the Microsoft contract, "expected to be secured by the GPUs the Group proposes to utilize to service, and the cash flows to be generated from, the Microsoft Agreement." Not yet executed/drawn as of Mar 31, 2026.

BANKRUPTCY-REMOTE / NON-RECOURSE SPV HISTORY: IREN previously used "Non-Recourse SPVs" (IE CA 3 Holdings Ltd., IE CA 4 Holdings Ltd.) for NYDIG limited-recourse equipment-financing loans; those SPVs defaulted and went into receivership/bankruptcy (PwC trustee) and were DECONSOLIDATED in FY2023. IREN settled all related claims with NYDIG in Aug 2025 for a $20M payment. No bankruptcy-remote SPV is part of current debt; current convertible notes are senior unsecured obligations of IREN Limited (parent), and the prepaid-forward/capped-call hedges are separate transactions.

DEBT STRUCTURE: As of Mar 31, 2026 interest-bearing debt = convertible notes payable carrying value $3,687.832M ($3,745.7M aggregate principal across 2029 3.50%, 2030 3.25%, 2031 0.00%, 2032 0.25%, 2033 1.00% senior convertible notes) plus $274.256M finance leases. No term loans/revolvers drawn. $0 of convertible notes due within one year. Low cash coupon (notes 0%-3.5%) keeps interest expense modest (~$40M TTM) despite ~$3.96B debt.

PROFITABILITY/QUALITY FLAG: FY2025 was profitable (operating income +$17.3M, net income +$86.9M, EBITDA $278.2M). But in FY2026 the company swung to a large operating LOSS (operating loss $426.3M for 9mo to Mar 31, 2026; $233.5M operating loss in Q3 alone), driven by $188.4M of asset impairments (Bitcoin miners/equipment displaced by the AI pivot) and a surge in SG&A/stock-based comp ($162.1M SBC). TTM operating income is therefore a ~$408M LOSS. TTM net income is positive (+$158M) ONLY because of a $533.9M non-cash unrealized GAIN on financial instruments (capped-call/prepaid-forward derivatives); on an operating basis the business is currently loss-making.

As the data centers are placed in service, capitalized interest will roll into the P&L, materially increasing reported interest expense going forward.
